gexcst.py.summary: Extract the functions, classes and constants of Python sources into separate files.
details: Walks the given files, directories and archives (``.whl``, ``.zip``, ``.tar*``, ``.zst``) with a LibCST-based extractor and writes every entity to ``output/`` with a unique name, keeping the source text intact. Files are handled in a worker pool.

gext.py.summary: Split Python sources into ``output/classes``, ``output/functions`` and ``output/const`` files.
details: Parses each module with :mod:`ast`, writes every top-level class, function and constant into its own file under ``output/`` and skips ``test``/``examples`` directories plus the output tree itself. The files are processed in a worker pool.

gext0.py.summary: Extract Python entities from files and archives into ``output/``.
details: Like :mod:`gexcst` but AST-based: functions, classes and constants of every scanned source (plain files, directories and archives) are written to ``output/`` with collision-free names.

git_repo_creator.py.summary: Create a GitHub repository and push the current project into it.
details: Two backends: ``api`` talks to the REST API with a token from ``--token``/``--env-file``, ``gh`` shells out to the GitHub CLI. Both initialise git when needed, optionally add a README and ``.gitignore``, stage and commit, set the remote and push the chosen branch.

gitclone.py.summary: Clone a git repository, fetching submodules when it has any.
details: Clones into the directory named after the repository (``--recursive`` is added when the remote advertises submodules), reports the default branch and exits with the status of ``git clone``.

gittools.py.summary: Bulk git chores: scan local changes, pull all clones, create repositories, edit ``.gitignore``.
details: ``scan-changes`` reports the status of every repository below a path, ``pull-all`` fast-forwards all of them in parallel, ``newrepo`` creates a GitHub repository through the API and pushes to it (with an optional ``--env-file`` token) and ``gitignore-add`` appends a line to the ``.gitignore`` files it finds.

gsz.py.summary: Print the size of a GitHub repository.
details: Accepts ``owner/repo`` or a full ``https://github.com/...`` URL, asks the GitHub API for the repository metadata and prints the size in megabytes.

hformat.py.summary: Re-indent HTML files with BeautifulSoup's pretty printer.
details: Parses each file (the arguments, or every ``.html`` file below the current directory) and rewrites it with ``soup.prettify()`` only when the formatting changed. Files are handled in parallel.

hijri.py.summary: Print today's date in the Jalali calendar with Persian digits.
details: Converts the current Gregorian date to Jalali with the classic day-number algorithm and prints the Persian weekday, day, month name and year (through ``faprint`` for right-to-left rendering).
Reads the history file, keeps the first occurrence of every command in order and rewrites the file, printing how many lines were removed.

html_entity.py.summary: Replace HTML entities with their characters in text files.
details: Substitutes a built-in table of entities (``<``, ``>``, ``&``, `` ``, ``©`` ...) and rewrites the matching files in place, in parallel.

html_minify_py.py.summary: Minify HTML files in place with lxml.
details: Parses the document with lxml, drops comments, collapses whitespace between tags and optionally removes attribute quotes before rewriting the file. ``HTMLMinifier`` exposes the same transformation as a class.

htmltomarkdown.py.summary: Convert an HTML file to Markdown.
details: Builds a small document tree from the HTML and renders the supported tags (headings, lists, links, images, emphasis, tables, pre/code blocks with language detection) as Markdown.

htmltools.py.summary: Inline, bundle and stand-alone HTML assets with one CLI.
details: ``bundle`` extracts the CSS/JS/images of a page and rebuilds a single ``single_page_local.html``, ``inline`` embeds local and remote assets directly into existing HTML/CSS, ``isolate`` writes ``<name>_standalone.html``, ``standalone`` does the same in parallel with a remote cache, ``mhtml`` unpacks ``.mhtml`` archives and ``css`` inlines ``@import`` rules and fonts. Options control the output directories, timeouts, user agent and the maximum download size.
